leads.submission: Prof. Dr. Simone Graeff-Hönninger, 5 October 2026, physical PDF page 4 / printed page 3, section 3.1; summary physical page 2 / printed page 1
leads.exact_draft: BT 21/2116, 7 October 2025; official archived sixteen-page bill
leads.suspicion: The claim that accidental THC exceedance in certified-seed crops leads to harvest disqualification and total loss supports raising the national threshold to 1%. Official government answer 21/1188, page 2, says the alternative certified-seed route absorbs natural THC fluctuations.
leads.checks: Read the complete eight-page author text plus cover, exact bill and government answer, current KCanG definition, BLE January 2026 farmer guidance and its January 2025 Annex 4. Independent energy reviewer read the same primary sources.
leads.why_unresolved: A formal certified-seed exemption is a serious qualification, but practical crop usability, product rules, enforcement or other loss mechanisms may remain. BLE permits harvest after sampling or written release but does not resolve subsequent high-THC outcomes. Silence is not proof of no destruction risk. The author separately acknowledges that the EU funding threshold remains unchanged, so no funding conflation is proved.
